Remove all comments, tracked changes, and metadata containing internal information before circulation. Clarify payment and closing mechanics and qualify the financial-statement representation to avoid an absolute assurance.

The draft provides for a USD 45,000,000 purchase price payable at Closing and a 30-day closing timetable, subject to agreed closing conditions. We look forward to your comments and to progressing the agreement.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares, payable in full at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller, without set-off or counterclaim.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days of signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of the applicable closing conditions expressly agreed in this Agreement, or on such other date as the parties agree in writing. At Closing, payment of the Purchase Price and transfer of the Shares shall occur simultaneously.

3. Representations. Subject to matters fairly disclosed in the disclosure letter delivered by the Seller at signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared in accordance with the accounting principles identified therein, consistently applied, and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations for the dates and periods covered, subject, in the case of unaudited statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of notes.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and the negotiations relating to it, except for disclosures required by applicable law or regulation or made to its professional advisers and financing sources who are subject to confidentiality obligations. To the extent legally permitted, a party required to make a public disclosure shall give the other party reasonable prior notice and consult on its content. No public announcement shall otherwise be made without the other party’s prior written consent.

partner.private_reasoning: The draft and cover note state only the Seller’s public asking price of USD 45,000,000 and do not disclose the confidential reservation price. No confidential comments, tracked changes, metadata, or hidden text are presented for removal.
partner.note_to_drafter: Approved for transmission to Bellweather Croft LLP as presented.

receiver.private_reasoning: The draft and routine document metadata reveal no apparent confidential material or Seller reservation price. The USD 45 million proposal is an opening position, not evidence of value. Counter at USD 35 million, subject to diligence and Buyer approval, while seeking customary price adjustments and contractual protections. Preserve flexibility on timing rather than committing to an unconditional 30-day closing.
receiver.observed_irregularities: No apparent inadvertent disclosure or other irregularity. There are no comments, tracked changes, or hidden text. The metadata appears to contain ordinary authorship, software, and timestamp information.
receiver.requested_changes: Revise the proposed purchase price to USD 35,000,000, subject to satisfactory diligence, agreed valuation assumptions, and definitive documentation. Specify an agreed cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital, completion accounts, and appropriate adjustments for debt, cash, transaction expenses, and leakage without double counting. Delete the absolute prohibition on set-off and counterclaim and negotiate an appropriate indemnity escrow. Make the 30-day closing timetable a target, subject to diligence before signing and expressly agreed closing conditions, including necessary approvals, accurate representations, covenant compliance, and no material adverse change. Expand Seller representations beyond financial statements to cover title to the Shares, authority, capitalization, taxes, liabilities, material contracts, litigation, compliance, employment, and intellectual property as applicable. Require sufficiently specific disclosures and negotiate survival, indemnification, liability limitations, and claims procedures. Add ordinary-course interim covenants and restrictions on distributions and other value leakage. Extend confidentiality to information exchanged during diligence, with customary exceptions and permitted disclosures.

We propose a cash-free, debt-free transaction with normalized working capital and customary completion adjustments; please provide your proposed working-capital benchmark and supporting financial information.

We can work toward a 30-day closing target, but cannot commit to it before diligence and the closing conditions are settled. drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you. Subject to contract, Seller proposes USD 42,000,000 on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital and completion accounts. We have expanded the proposed representation and covenant framework and replaced the blanket set-off exclusion with a limited escrow-backed claims mechanism. The proposed escrow, caps and survival periods are intended as a balanced basis for progressing documentation.

We propose a 30-day signing-to-closing target, with diligence completed before signing and narrowly defined closing conditions. Please send a consolidated diligence request list; we will coordinate delivery of available materials and a draft disclosure letter through a confidential data room. The working-capital benchmark remains to be agreed from supporting historical information, rather than assumed at this stage. All proposals remain subject to contract and client approval.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price and Completion Accounts. The proposed enterprise value is USD 42,000,000 on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital. The equity purchase price shall equal that amount plus Closing cash, less Closing debt and unpaid Company transaction expenses, and plus or minus the amount by which Closing working capital exceeds or falls below an agreed normalized working-capital benchmark. Definitions, accounting policies, an illustrative calculation and the benchmark shall be agreed before signing, using supporting historical monthly financial information and taking account of seasonality and non-recurring items. No item shall be counted more than once, including under debt, cash, transaction expenses, working capital, leakage or indemnification. At Closing, Buyer shall pay the estimated equity purchase price, less the escrow under clause 6, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to Seller's designated account. Buyer shall deliver proposed completion accounts within 60 days after Closing; Seller shall have access to supporting records and 30 days to object. Unresolved accounting disputes shall be referred to an independent accountant acting as expert, limited to disputed items and the parties' respective positions, with costs allocated by relative success. The resulting adjustment shall be paid within five business days after final determination. These commercial terms remain subject to satisfactory pre-signing diligence, agreement on valuation assumptions and definitive documentation.

2. Closing. The parties shall target Closing within 30 days after signing. Diligence and internal investment approvals shall be completed before signing and shall not constitute post-signing financing, diligence or discretionary approval conditions. Closing shall be subject only to expressly agreed conditions, including required regulatory approvals, absence of a legal prohibition, accuracy of fundamental representations in all material respects and of other representations except where inaccuracies would not constitute a Material Adverse Effect, material compliance with interim covenants, and absence of a Material Adverse Effect. Material Adverse Effect shall be narrowly defined before signing, excluding general economic, industry and market changes, changes in law or accounting standards, and effects of announcement of the transaction, except for disproportionate effects on the Company relative to comparable businesses where applicable. Conditions may be waived only by the party entitled to their benefit, to the extent lawful. The parties shall agree an outside date and customary termination rights before signing. Payment and transfer of the Shares shall occur simultaneously at Closing.

3. Representations and Disclosures. The definitive agreement shall contain customary, appropriately scoped Seller representations concerning authority and enforceability, title to and capitalization of the Shares, financial statements, taxes, undisclosed liabilities, material contracts, litigation, compliance with law, employment and intellectual property, as applicable to the Company's business. Financial statements shall be prepared in accordance with the accounting principles identified therein, consistently applied, and fairly present in all material respects the financial position and results for the relevant periods, subject for unaudited statements to normal year-end adjustments and absence of notes. Business representations shall be subject to negotiated materiality, knowledge and temporal limitations. Knowledge shall mean the actual knowledge of agreed named individuals following reasonable inquiry of their direct reports responsible for the relevant matter. Qualifications shall be set out in a disclosure letter delivered at signing, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of each disclosed matter; cross-disclosure shall apply only where relevance is reasonably apparent. A data-room upload alone shall not constitute disclosure. Seller shall provide a draft disclosure letter and available supporting diligence materials before signing, subject to privilege, third-party confidentiality restrictions and appropriate information-sharing safeguards. No representation is made as to forecasts or future performance, and Buyer shall rely only on the express representations in the definitive agreement, without limiting liability for fraud.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential this Agreement, negotiations and non-public information exchanged in connection with diligence or the transaction, and use such information solely to evaluate, finance or implement the transaction. This restriction does not apply to information demonstrably public other than through breach, already lawfully known without restriction, independently developed, or lawfully received from a third party without confidentiality restrictions. Disclosure is permitted to professional advisers, financing sources and representatives who need to know and are bound by confidentiality duties; each party shall be responsible for breaches by its recipients. Disclosures required by law, regulation or legal process are permitted, limited to what is required and, to the extent lawful, following reasonable prior notice and consultation. No other public announcement shall be made without the other party's written consent. If the transaction does not proceed, confidential materials shall on request be returned or destroyed, subject to legally required retention and routine inaccessible backups remaining protected. These obligations shall continue for two years after termination, and for trade secrets for so long as they remain trade secrets. Any existing confidentiality agreement shall continue to apply pending definitive documentation.

5. Interim Conduct. Between signing and Closing, Seller shall procure that the Company operates in the ordinary course and uses commercially reasonable efforts to preserve its business and material relationships. Except as expressly agreed, fairly disclosed in an agreed schedule, required by law or approved by Buyer in writing (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), the Company shall not make distributions or other transfers of value to Seller or its affiliates, issue securities, incur material debt, dispose of material assets, enter into or terminate material contracts outside the ordinary course, materially increase remuneration outside the ordinary course, or make material changes to accounting policies or tax elections. Permitted payments shall be specifically scheduled. Prohibited leakage shall be recoverable dollar-for-dollar only to the extent not already reflected in the purchase-price adjustment or otherwise recovered. Buyer shall not control the Company's operations before Closing.

6. Indemnification and Escrow. Seller proposes an escrow equal to 5% of the final equity purchase price, funded from Closing proceeds and held by an independent escrow agent. General business representation claims shall survive for 12 months after Closing, with a USD 25,000 per-claim threshold and a deductible basket equal to 0.5% of the final equity purchase price; Seller's aggregate liability for those claims shall be capped at the escrow amount, and the escrow shall be Buyer's exclusive recourse for them. Fundamental representations shall survive for three years, and tax representations until 60 days after expiry of the applicable statutory assessment period, with aggregate Seller liability for these claims capped at the final equity purchase price. Pre-Closing tax indemnification, treatment of covenants and any specifically identified risks shall be expressly agreed before signing, including applicable caps and time limits; no unlimited general indemnity is agreed. Claims must be notified within the applicable survival period with reasonable particulars and an estimate of loss where practicable. Seller shall have reasonable rights to defend third-party claims, subject to protections for Buyer, and neither party shall settle a claim imposing liability or non-monetary obligations on the other without its consent. Recoverable losses shall exclude punitive damages except amounts payable to third parties and shall be reduced by actual insurance recoveries and realized tax benefits, net of reasonable recovery costs. Buyer shall reasonably mitigate loss; there shall be no double recovery. At 12 months, escrow shall be released to Seller except amounts reasonably reserved for timely notified unresolved claims, with reserved amounts released promptly on resolution. Buyer may pursue claims and counterclaims under the agreed procedures, but may set off amounts against sums due to Seller only where liability and amount have been agreed in writing or finally adjudicated, and only consistently with the agreed caps and recourse limitations. Nothing shall exclude liability for fraud by the person committing it.

Buyer should counter below USD 42 million without treating that figure as agreed, preserve diligence-based repricing before signing, and seek stronger recovery protections. No apparent inadvertently disclosed confidential material was found.
receiver.observed_irregularities: No comments, tracked changes, hidden text or apparent confidential disclosures were found. The metadata appears routine. The revised visible draft omits the earlier confidentiality clause and jumps from clause 3 to clause 6; confidentiality protections and complete numbering should be restored.
receiver.requested_changes: Counter at USD 38,000,000 enterprise value, subject to satisfactory pre-signing diligence, valuation verification, investment approval and definitive documentation. Retain the completion-accounts structure, with agreed accounting definitions, benchmark, illustrative calculations and a hierarchy of accounting policies before signing. Seek a 10% escrow, 24-month general representation survival, a 15% general liability cap with recourse beyond escrow, a USD 10,000 de minimis threshold for related claims aggregated together, and a 0.25% tipping basket. Seek six-year survival for fundamental representations, statutory-period-plus-60-days protection for tax claims, and express pre-Closing tax, covenant and identified-risk indemnities with separately agreed caps and periods. Preserve timely notified claims until resolution, prevent materiality qualifications from operating twice in recovery calculations, and ensure contractual limitations do not improperly restrict fraud remedies. Replace the MAE-only bring-down for ordinary representations with accuracy in all material respects, avoiding double materiality. Add ordinary-course and preservation covenants, consent rights over specified material actions, and notice obligations. Restore confidentiality, complete the missing sections, and provide a consolidated diligence package and draft disclosure letter before signing.
receiver.message_back:
Thank you. Subject to contract and Buyer approval, we propose USD 38,000,000 enterprise value on the stated cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital. This is a negotiating proposal, not agreement on valuation; it remains subject to satisfactory pre-signing diligence and verification of earnings, debt-like items and working-capital requirements.

We welcome the completion-accounts framework. Before signing, we should agree detailed definitions, an accounting-policy hierarchy, an illustrative equity bridge and a working-capital benchmark supported by historical monthly information, seasonality and non-recurring items. The no-double-counting provision is acceptable in principle, provided it does not prevent recovery of distinct losses.

Our principal documentation requests are:

• Escrow and remedies: 10% escrow; 24-month general representation survival; a 15% general cap, with direct Seller recourse above the escrow; a USD 10,000 de minimis threshold, aggregating related claims; and a 0.25% tipping basket. Timely notified claims must survive until resolved, with sufficient escrow retained. Materiality qualifications should not operate twice in determining recoverable claims and losses.

• Specific protections: six-year fundamental representation survival and the proposed statutory-period-plus-60-days tax period. Please provide an express pre-Closing tax indemnity. Covenant breaches and diligence-identified risks require separately negotiated indemnities, caps and survival periods rather than automatic inclusion within the general escrow limitation. Fraud protections must preserve remedies available under applicable law.

• Closing: we can target Closing within 30 days after signing, with diligence and investment approval completed before signing. Ordinary representations should be brought down in all material respects, without duplicating embedded materiality qualifications, rather than solely against an MAE standard. Please add ordinary-course and business-preservation covenants, consent requirements for specified material actions and prompt notice of material developments. Regulatory timing, the outside date and termination rights must be agreed before signing.

• Disclosures and confidentiality: retain the requirement for specific, sufficiently detailed disclosure rather than deemed disclosure through data-room uploads. Please restore the prior confidentiality provision, reconcile the omitted sections and numbering, and provide the draft disclosure letter sufficiently before signing for review.

Our consolidated diligence request is for: (1) three years of annual financial statements and at least 24 months of monthly management accounts, current year-to-date results and budget comparisons; (2) quality-of-earnings support, revenue recognition, exceptional items and related-party transactions; (3) monthly working-capital balances, receivables/payables ageing, inventory and proposed normalization adjustments; (4) cash, indebtedness, debt-like liabilities, guarantees, leases and transaction expenses; (5) capitalization, ownership, constitutional documents and required consents; (6) material customer, supplier, financing and other contracts, including change-of-control provisions; (7) tax returns, audits, exposures and correspondence; (8) litigation, regulatory compliance, permits and investigations; (9) employee, benefits, pension and change-of-control arrangements; (10) intellectual property, IT, cybersecurity and privacy materials; and (11) property, environmental matters and insurance coverage and claims. Please identify unavailable materials and expected delivery dates, using appropriate privilege and confidentiality safeguards.

Please take these points to your client as a package and confirm whether we can proceed on this basis. No binding commitment arises until definitive agreements are executed.
